channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Bessent Gives Nvidia Ten Days to Answer Export Questions and Calls for an Outside Chief
item.description: The United States Treasury Secretary has told Nvidia its board and outside lawyers must answer questions about export-control compliance within ten days, and said the chipmaker should hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

item.title: Houthis Free 600 Detainees in Sanaa in Largest Unilateral Release of Yemen War
item.description: Yemen's Houthi authorities have freed 600 people detained in connection with the country's war, in a unilateral release in the capital Sanaa confirmed by the Red Cross, as fighting intensified in the south of the country.

item.title: Huge Crowds Fill Prague Park to Defend Public Media From Funding Overhaul
item.description: Tens of thousands of Czechs filled Letna Park in Prague on Sunday to protest a government plan to scrap the fee that pays for public television and radio and fund the broadcasters from the state budget instead, a change critics say would put their independence at risk.

item.title: Israel Vows Gaza Offensive Will Continue as Hamas Appeals for Winter Aid and Ceasefire Frays
item.description: Israel's defence minister has said the offensive in Gaza will go on until the territory is demilitarised and Hamas is gone, as Hamas's political chief appealed to Arab and Muslim countries to act and aid agencies warned that winter floods are endangering hundreds of thousands of displaced people.

item.title: Supertanker Loaded With Two Million Barrels of Oil Sinks After Mine Strike, Iran Says
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a supertanker loaded with more than two million barrels of crude oil sank after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, one of two tankers they say struck mines on an unauthorised route.

item.title: Drones Strike Three Ships Off Romania's Black Sea Coast, Jets Scrambled Twice
item.description: Three commercial vessels have been hit by drones off Romania's Black Sea coast near the Sulina canal, and Romania scrambled fighter jets twice in response. No one was hurt, and the crews put out the fires on board.

item.title: Bomb Threat Wave Sweeps Europe, Emptying Schools, Diverting Flights and Clearing Newsrooms
item.description: A wave of bomb threats sent mainly by email has forced evacuations at thousands of schools, diverted passenger flights and emptied newsrooms across Europe, even though every threat checked so far has turned out to be false.

item.title: Estonia to Shut All Russia Border Crossings From December 1 After Drone Maker Attack
item.description: Estonia will close all three of its border crossings with Russia from 1 December, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced on Sunday, after an attempted arson at a drone maker that Tallinn blames on Russian military intelligence.

item.title: Somalia Says International Support Saved It as UN Mission Closes and Peacekeeper Funding Falters
item.description: Somalia's foreign affairs minister says his country would not have recovered from three decades of conflict without the international community, as the United Nations closes its political mission and funding for African peacekeepers runs into trouble.

item.title: Bangladesh Measles Death Toll Reaches 1,314 as Eight More Children Die
item.description: Eight more children have died in Bangladesh's measles outbreak, taking the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-linked deaths in the country this year to 1,314.

item.title: Canadian Soldier Becomes Fifth Death From Wainwright Training Fire
item.description: The death toll from the fire that swept a Canadian army training ground last month has risen to five, after a soldier who had been in hospital since the blaze died on Friday, the military said.

item.title: Fire Sweeps Through Syrian Refugee Camp in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley, Leaving Hundreds Homeless
item.description: A fire swept through a Syrian refugee camp in the town of Bar Elias in eastern Lebanon on Saturday, destroying dozens of tents and leaving hundreds of people without shelter, as firefighters brought the blaze under control.

item.title: Bay of Bengal Depression Set to Become Cyclone Akvan as Andhra Coast Goes on Alert
item.description: A depression over the Bay of Bengal is strengthening into a cyclone likely to be named Akvan, with India's east coast on alert for heavy rain and winds of up to 145 kilometres per hour as the system heads towards Andhra Pradesh.

item.title: Bilawal Condemns 'Political Victimisation' of JUI-F in Call With Fazlur Rehman
item.description: Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has condemned what he called political victimisation of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl, telling its chief, Maulana Fazlur Rehman, in a telephone call that the government must tolerate opposition criticism and stop turning political differences into revenge.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Starshield Speed Limits Are Letting Russian Strikes Through
item.description: Ukraine's president has blamed speed limits on the military satellite internet service Starshield for allowing Russian attacks on the country's energy network to succeed, saying interceptor drones are losing contact with their operators mid-flight.

item.title: Bahrain Holds Iran Responsible for Drone Attacks and Rejects Being a Battleground in Its Feud With the US
item.description: Bahrain has formally held Iran responsible for Sunday's drone attacks on the island and rejected the use of its territory to settle scores with the United States, as American forces said they shot down two of the incoming drones.

item.title: Common Diabetes Drug Metformin Linked to Lower Death Risk After Covid, Study Finds
item.description: People with type 2 diabetes who were taking the common drug metformin before catching Covid-19 were far more likely to still be alive a year later than patients on a different diabetes drug, new research suggests.

item.title: Three Men Sentenced to Death in Jordan for Church Shooting That Killed Nine
item.description: A court in Jordan on Sunday handed down death sentences to three men over a gun attack on a church funeral in the south of the country last month that killed nine people and wounded 34.

item.title: Houthis Seize Kharaz Base in Lahj as Advance Closes In on Aden
item.description: Houthi fighters seized the strategic Kharaz military base in the southern province of Lahj early on Sunday, pushing closer to the port city of Aden after government troops were forced to retreat.

item.title: Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left the Company in August 2025
item.description: Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang left the firm on 30 August 2025 and holds no position there, as scrutiny grows over its purchases of advanced Nvidia chips in the scandal that forced Nvidia founder Jensen Huang to resign last week.

item.title: Australia Beat New Zealand 32-12 to Win Rugby League World Cup for 13th Time
item.description: Australia beat New Zealand 32-12 in the Rugby League World Cup final in Brisbane on Sunday, winning the title for a 13th time and a fourth tournament in a row.

item.title: Nearly 1,500 Migrants Reach Canary Islands in a Single Day, the Most Since 2020
item.description: Almost 1,500 migrants arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands on Saturday, the highest number in a single day since 2020, after the coastguard rescued them from 14 boats, the EFE news agency reported.

item.title: Four Hurt and Two Brothers Held as Israeli Forces Raid Balata Camp in Nablus
item.description: Four Palestinians were hurt and two brothers were arrested during an Israeli raid on the Balata refugee camp in Nablus on Sunday, medics said, in the latest incursion into the occupied West Bank city.

item.title: Iraq's Prime Minister Sacks Nine Officials in Oil Smuggling Crackdown on Militia Stronghold
item.description: Iraq's prime minister has dismissed nine senior security and oil officials and ordered suspects to face the courts, after an investigation found organised oil smuggling in a district controlled by one of the country's most powerful Iran-aligned armed groups.

item.title: 500 Million Indians Left Poverty Behind — but Millions Still Live on the Edge
item.description: A new World Bank report credits India with moving almost 500 million people above the poverty line during the 12 years to 2023 — yet millions who crossed it still live a single shock away from falling back.

item.title: Spain Coach Insists 'There Is No Racism' in Spain as Yamal and Vinicius Say Otherwise
item.description: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente insisted on Saturday that there is no racism in Spain, a day before his side face England in Madrid, despite his own star players saying they have repeatedly suffered racist abuse in the country.

item.title: Zardari and Shehbaz Agree Parliament Must Approve Any Vote on New Provinces
item.description: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have agreed that any move to create new provinces — including a proposed public referendum — must go through parliament, according to officials briefed on their meeting in Lahore on Saturday.

item.title: Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Munir Share Top Spot in Global Muslim Influence Ranking
item.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir have jointly taken the top spot in the latest ranking of the world's 500 most influential Muslims, sharing the number one position with three other leaders in a first for the annual list.

item.title: Hamas Rafah Commander Killed in Overnight Israeli Strike in Southern Gaza
item.description: Hamas has confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah Brigade, was killed in an Israeli air strike overnight in southern Gaza, a killing the Israeli military also confirmed on Sunday morning.

item.title: ASEAN Summit Opens in Manila as Leaders Weigh Energy Crisis and Regional Tensions
item.description: Southeast Asian leaders opened the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila on Sunday, gathering in the Philippine capital to confront an energy crisis sharpened by the war in the Middle East, tensions in the South China Sea and Myanmar's long civil conflict.
